content.text: This report has been prepared pursuant to Standing Order 109 (3), (4), (5) and (6) of Dáil Éireann, and Standing Order 86 (6) of Seanad Éireann which provide for the Joint Committee to-
undertake a review of its procedure and its role generally;
lay minutes of its proceedings before both Houses;
make an annual report to both Houses.
At its meeting on the 11 February 2026, the Joint Committee agreed that all these items should be included in this report covering the period from May 2025 to December 2025.

The Dáil Select Committee was established by Order of Dáil Éireann of 30 April 2025 to consider Bills, Estimates for Public Services, Motions, and the terms of any international agreement involving a charge on public funds, which come within the aegis of the Department of Children, Disability and Equality.
The Select Committee may also consider Annual Output Statements, Value for Money Reviews and Policy Reviews prepared by the Department of Children, Disability and Equality.

The Dáil Select Committee, under the same Order, was enjoined with a Select Committee of Seanad Éireann, established by Order of Seanad Éireann of 29 April 2025, to form the Joint Committee on Disability Matters
Among the principal functions of the Joint Committee are to consider—
public affairs administered by the Department of Children, Disability and Equality;
matters of policy for which the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality is responsible;
legislative and expenditure proposals of the Department of Children, Disability and Equality;
Certain matters relating to bodies under the aegis of the Department of Children, Disability and Equality.
The Terms of Reference of the Dáil Select Committee and the Joint Committee are set out in our related information section.

Dáil Standing Order 113 (2) provides for a proportion of Cathaoirligh to be allocated to each group by means of the D’Hondt System. Deputy Maurice Quinlivan was appointed as Cathaoirleach of the Select Committee on 07 May 2025 by an Order of Dáil Éireann. The Cathaoirleach of the Select Committee is also the Cathaoirleach of the Joint Committee. Senator Margaret Murphy O'Mahony was elected as Leas-Chathaoirleach of the Joint Committee on the 21 May 2025.

Meetings of the Joint Committee and Select Committee took place in the Committee rooms in Leinster House 2000 and through Microsoft Teams. Meetings were in public unless otherwise ordered by the Committee.

Committee proceedings were broadcast live within Leinster House and also made available to RTÉ, Virgin Media and TG4. Proceedings were also live streamed on our website and through our app. Since September 2014 the proceedings of Committees in public session, typically recorded but occasionally live, are broadcast on the dedicated parliamentary channel Oireachtas TV which is available on these channels:
Saorview 22, Sky 514, Virgin Media 207, eir Vision 504
An Official Report (Parliamentary Debates) of the public meetings of the Committee may be viewed on the Houses of the Oireachtas website at
Copies of other reports published by the Joint Committee are also available on the
. A list of these reports is set out at paragraph 7.
The Joint Committee met on 24 occasions during the period under report. The number of hours of discussion involved in these meetings was in excess of 45 hours and 35 minutes.
The subject matter of each meeting of the Joint Committee, including the groups, organisations or individuals who attended the meetings, is detailed in
. The Minutes of Proceedings of the Joint Committee in public session are attached at
The Dáil Select Committee met once during the period under report and the number of hours of discussion involved in this meeting was 1 hour 36 minutes.
The subject matter of that meeting, including the groups, organisations or individuals who attended the meeting of the Select Committee, is detailed in
. The proceedings (Imeachtaí) of the Select Committee are attached at
During the period, the number of speaking witnesses for each of the Committees was as follows:
During the period under report, the Joint Committee published two reports, i.e. the Work Programme 2025 and the Review of the Joint Committee on Autism Final Report.
The Committee did not undertake any travel during the reporting period.
From May to December 2025, the Joint Committee did not consider any EU legislative proposals. There were no EU Scrutiny committee report(s) laid during this period.
There were no EU Council meetings held during this period.
Six-Monthly Report(s) on Developments within the EU
There were no Reports during this period.
The Joint Committee is currently satisfied with its present procedures and role.

Minutes of Meeting of Thursday, 15 May 2025
The Joint Committee met in Public Session at 09.33 a.m. in Committee Room 1, LH 2000, a quorum being present.
Deputies: Martin Daly, Seamus Healy, Keira Keogh, Claire Kerrane, Liam Quaide, Maurice Quinlivan (Cathaoirleach), Gillian Toole
Senators: Maria Byrne, Tom Clonan, Margaret Murphy O'Mahony
The topic for the meeting was
In accordance with Standing Orders, the Cathaoirleach read the declaration.

The Cathaoirleach advised Members that they might wish to consult with one another regarding nominations for the position of Leas-Chathaoirleach and proposed that members send nominations to the Clerk by close of business on 19 May 2025.
The Committee went into Private Session at 09.38 a.m.
This meeting adjourned at 10.11 a.m., and the next meeting will be at
9.30am, Wednesday 21 May 2025 when the Committee will meet in public session.
Minutes of Meeting of Wednesday, 21 May 2025
The Joint Committee met in Public Session at 09.32 a.m. in Committee Room 1, LH 2000, a quorum being present.
Deputies: Micheál Carrigy, Seamus Healy, Keira Keogh, Claire Kerrane, Paul McAuliffe, Liam Quaide, Maurice Quinlivan (Cathaoirleach), Gillian Toole
Senators: Nikki Bradley, Laura Harmon, Margaret Murphy O'Mahony
The topic for the meeting was
In accordance with Standing Orders, the Cathaoirleach read the declaration.
The Cathaoirleach noted that, as agreed at the committee's first meeting, a nomination for the position of Leas-Chathaoirleach was received—Senator Margaret Murphy O'Mahony.

The Cathaoirleach then invited any other nominations for the position of Leas-Chathaoirleach. Receiving none, the Cathaoirleach proposed Senator Margaret Murphy O'Mahony's election as Leas-Chathaoirleach of the Joint Committee.
The Cathaoirleach declared that Senator Margaret Murphy O’Mahony be elected as Leas-Chathaoirleach. The Cathaoirleach congratulated the newly elected Leas-Chathaoirleach.
The Committee went into Private Session at 09.35 a.m.
This meeting adjourned at 10.13 a.m., and the next meeting will be at
